look_here_first: Start with the UPPER surfaces of the upper leaves and white-margined bracts. Snow-on-the-mountain is usually mostly glabrous above and has broader elliptic to obovate white-margined bracts; then confirm with its hairy ovary/capsule. The white display is bract tissue, not petals.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbia: milky latex and a cyathium instead of an ordinary petaled flower. The conspicuous white areas are primarily bracts plus gland appendages.
morphology_keys.growth_form: Annual, erect herb with a conspicuously white-topped flowering canopy.
morphology_keys.leaves: Distal leaves and bracts become conspicuously white-margined; the showiest upper bracts are relatively broad.
morphology_keys.pubescence: Upper leaf surfaces are mostly glabrous. Hairiness can still occur on lower surfaces, along the midrib, peduncles, cyathia, ovary, and capsule, so 'the whole plant is hairless' is not a safe rule.
morphology_keys.bracts: Largest white-margined bracts are generally broader, commonly elliptic to obovate, rather than the long narrow linear-to-narrowly-oblanceolate bracts of E. bicolor.
morphology_keys.cyathium: Flower-like cyathia bear pale glands with conspicuous white appendages.
morphology_keys.fruit: Three-lobed capsule, conspicuously hairy; detailed Williamson treatment gives capsules about 4.5–5 × 7–7.5 mm.
morphology_keys.seed: Seeds about 4.5 × 3 mm in the detailed Williamson treatment, with minute tuberculate/netlike surface patterning.
best_field_traits: erect annual with conspicuous white-margined distal leaves/bracts
upper leaf and bract surfaces mostly glabrous
largest showy bracts relatively broad, typically elliptic to obovate
white display consists of modified bracts/gland appendages rather than ordinary petals
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Against E. bicolor, use two linked characters: E. marginata is generally broader-bracted and glabrous on the upper leaf/bract surfaces; E. bicolor is narrower-bracted and conspicuously hairy above.

lookalike_matrix.Euphorbia bicolor: linear to narrowly oblanceolate; longer and narrower

lookalike_matrix.Euphorbia marginata: can still be hairy below, along midribs, peduncles, cyathia, ovary, and fruit
lookalike_matrix.Euphorbia bicolor: hairiness much more pervasive, including upper leaf/bract surfaces
lookalike_matrix.reliability: hair placement matters more than a vague impression of 'hairy'

comparisons.key_distinctions: Broad white-margined bracts PLUS mostly glabrous upper surfaces strongly favor E. marginata. Do not use the amount of white or overall height alone.
